name: Right-libertarianism
summary: Right-libertarianism holds that individuals fully own themselves and may acquire unowned resources by first use or labor, so that capitalist property rights and free markets are just and taxation and redistribution are rights violations. Governments should be abolished (anarcho-capitalists) or confined to a night-watchman role of courts, police and defense (minarchists). Most adherents favor legal drugs and sex work, non-interventionism abroad and an end to the welfare state, while splitting on immigration, abortion and cultural questions.
scope: The mainstream Rothbard-Nozick core as described by Wikipedia and the Stanford Encyclopedia: self-ownership, homesteading, the non-aggression principle, with minarchist (Nozick) and anarcho-capitalist (Rothbard) wings both counted. Left-libertarianism (common ownership of resources) is excluded, and the strands diverge on the state, immigration, abortion and culture, where answers are low confidence or neutral.

keyFigures.name: Murray Rothbard
keyFigures.role: Systematized anarcho-capitalism and popularized the term libertarian in the US.

keyFigures.name: Robert Nozick
keyFigures.role: Defended a minimal state in Anarchy, State, and Utopia.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Health care is a service to be bought and sold; state guarantees need taxation, which right-libertarians treat as a rights violation.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A wage floor overrides voluntary contracts between employer and worker, which they treat as coercive interference in free markets.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Right-libertarianism defends free markets, and most strands (Austrian and Chicago alike) hold that markets allocate better than state planning.

public-ownership.rationale: Capitalist private ownership is the core of the view; state ownership of industry is a coercive monopoly they would privatize.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Rothbard treats all taxation as forcible theft, so higher rates on anyone are a larger theft, not a fairer share.

unions-good.rationale: Voluntary unions are tolerated, but adherents are generally sceptical of unions' social value and of the legal privileges they receive.

property-fundamental.rationale: Wikipedia describes the view as holding that people have an absolute right to what their labor produces and to enforced private property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Concentrated economic power is acceptable when acquired by non-coercive means, so extra regulation of firms is itself an intrusion.

cut-welfare.rationale: The view calls for major reduction or abolition of the welfare state, which it holds is counter-productive as well as unjust.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers may form cooperatives voluntarily, but a general prescription of collective ownership is the anti-capitalist position left-libertarians hold and right-libertarians reject.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Rothbard stresses civil liberties against the state and holds that only invasion of person or property justifies force, so mass surveillance is not accepted.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Libertarians support legalizing victimless crimes such as marijuana use, and self-ownership grounds an objection to paternalism.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Rothbard protects speech, publishing and assembly as rights; speech is not aggression, so it should not be legally restricted.

strong-leader.rationale: A leader bypassing checks threatens the strict limits on government that the view demands.

state-harmful.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists say yes, but minarchists defend a night-watchman state as justified, so the mainstream is split and leans against calling it unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Strong self-ownership includes the right to defend oneself, and the state restricting peaceful possession invades property and person.

empower-police-military.rationale: Minarchists keep these functions as core duties but want them limited, and anarcho-capitalists would privatize them, so more funding and authority is not endorsed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Rothbard explicitly names prostitution among consensual victimless acts that are not crimes since no person or property is invaded.

decide-locally.rationale: Adherents prefer smaller, more decentralized government and secession as limits on power, though the sources do not state this as a doctrine.

rehabilitation.rationale: Rothbard's theory of justice centers on proportionate punishment and restitution to victims rather than reforming offenders; this is inferred and not universal.

traditional-family.rationale: Paleolibertarians praise traditional family while others are neutral or liberal, so adherents are split on social issues.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Most right-libertarians would let any adults contract a marriage, but social conservatives within the family dissent.

abortion-legal.rationale: Right-libertarians are split between those who treat it as a bodily-autonomy right and those who treat the fetus as a person.

more-religion-public.rationale: Early liberal separation of church and state is endorsed, and the state has no role promoting religion, though cultural conservatives differ.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Redress is owed only from identified wrongdoers to identified victims, and state programs funded by taxation are a coercive remedy.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The ideology is about rights and property, not the nature of gender, so there is no collective stance.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Paleolibertarians value national culture while others see culture as private and spontaneous, so adherents differ.

gradual-change.rationale: Rothbard demanded immediate abolition of aggression as a moral principle and rejected gradualism, though pragmatists accept incremental reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Right-libertarians are divided: some argue for open movement as free exchange, others like Hoppe argue for restriction as property owners.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Right-libertarians favor non-interventionism and hold that further supranational power is another coercive monopoly.

free-trade.rationale: Free exchange across borders follows from property and contract rights and is central to the market programme.

nation-first.rationale: They oppose nationalism and militarism as collectivist, though they also dislike global bodies, so the stance is mixed and leans against this.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Right-libertarians favor non-interventionism in foreign policy and treat war as mass killing financed by taxation.

open-borders.rationale: Adherents are divided on whether open borders follow from freedom of movement or violate the rights of property owners.

limit-growth.rationale: Economic growth through free exchange is a good, and limits imposed by the state conflict with property rights.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Drastic government action would require coercive regulation and taxation; they prefer property-rights remedies.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The market-optimist view expects innovation under free markets to solve problems, though this is inferred from general commitments.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Free-market advocates favor ending regulatory barriers to energy production, though many oppose public subsidies for it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Aggression by the state may be resisted, as in the American Revolution Rothbard celebrates, though adherents mostly stress peaceful means.

experts-over-public.rationale: Hayekian arguments hold that central expertise cannot replace dispersed knowledge, but neither would they give the public power over rights.

central-planning.rationale: The Austrian school central to the view holds that planning cannot calculate economically, and the view defends capitalist markets against planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The view accepts private ownership of industry as just; markets that rest on worker or state ownership are a different, left-libertarian or socialist position.

land-value-tax.rationale: Any tax is a taking, and right-libertarians reject the left-libertarian claim that appropriated land is owed to everyone.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Taxation is theft, and a legitimate owner may freely give property to heirs.

basic-income.rationale: A tax-funded unconditional income is redistribution they reject, though some, following Friedman, accept a negative income tax as a lesser evil.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: They hold that free trade is an exercise of property and contract rights and tariffs a tax and restriction on it.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of capital substitutes political for market allocation and is opposed on both rights and efficiency grounds.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Right-libertarians accept whatever distribution arises through non-coercive means, including concentrated holdings, and reject engineered dispersal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wage labor and money exchange are legitimate voluntary contracts in a capitalist order.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Austrian-school adherents favor ending central banking in favor of market money, though Chicago-school adherents differ.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies fixing wages and prices override voluntary contracting.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rule by a single party is the opposite of the strictly limited government they seek.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The view is about limited government rather than regime form, though a few like Hoppe prefer monarchy to democracy; most do not endorse hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: They see majority rule as no guarantee of rights, and some such as Hoppe criticize it, though minarchists accept constitutional democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: More direct majority voting increases the risk of rights being overridden by popular votes.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the basis of power replace property rights and the limited state with collective rule.

right-to-secede.rationale: If the state has no special moral status above other institutions, regions and individuals may leave it; this follows from the denial of its special right to coerce.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equal self-ownership and equal rights before the law leave no room for a natural entitlement to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Rothbard condemns the initiation of violence but not defensive force, so adherents do not say violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Rothbard calls modern war mass murder, and non-interventionists reject glorifying it.

separate-church-state.rationale: Right-libertarians list separation of state and religion among liberal aims and exclude state support for religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Enforcing scripture on adults would punish consensual acts without victims, which Rothbard denies is a crime.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rothbard argues courts and police could be supplied by competing private firms; anarcho-capitalists agree, while minarchists keep them public.

military-superiority.rationale: Right-libertarians generally oppose militarism and empire, though minarchists support adequate national defense.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The view is built on individual rights, with no entitlement to a nation defined by ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Austrian economists reject Marxist class struggle as the driver of history, though Rothbard held that a ruling class exploits through the state.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Redistribution toward equal outcomes is described as criminally immoral and counter-productive, since just holdings depend on how they were acquired.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Land goes to those who homestead or acquire it justly; whether specific indigenous claims meet that test divides adherents.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Redress is owed by actual wrongdoers to victims; charging present taxpayers is a coercive collective burden.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political unification into larger states multiplies coercive power; a union of civilizations has no basis in individual rights.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Objectivist and market-defence strands praise self-interest, while others only treat it as permissible, so it is not uniform.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Individual rights are the starting point of the doctrine, and rights are not subordinated to community duties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The doctrine concerns rights and property, with no standard view on intrinsic value of nature.

limit-population.rationale: Coercive population limits violate self-ownership and are an aggression.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Industrial capitalism is defended as the product of voluntary exchange and a great benefit.

accelerate-technology.rationale: They welcome market-driven innovation, though not as a state-led goal, so this is inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Self-ownership gives each person full rights over body, and a principled objection to paternalism.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Wider government decision-making by any means is opposed on limited-government grounds.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Privacy against state intrusion follows from civil liberties and the principle that the state may not invade persons or property.

restore-past-order.rationale: The programme is a principled rights doctrine, not a restorationist one, though paleolibertarians are nostalgic.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Nozick and Rothbard base policy on rights and entitlement, not outcomes alone, so ideology-free pragmatism is not accepted.

direct-action.rationale: Strands vary between electoral work, education and counter-economic agorism, so there is no common preference.

means-match-ends.rationale: Rothbard stresses principle in means but there is no common doctrine on this link.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Capitalist production and trade are held to benefit humanity.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The division of labor underlies market exchange and is defended.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Justice is historical entitlement, so distribution by need is redistribution that violates rights.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for profit under private ownership is the defended system.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Profit from non-coercive exchange is legitimate; the exploitation claim is rejected.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by one class over another by force is the opposite of the non-aggression principle.

collective-farming.rationale: Land is held by private owners, and compulsory collectivization is aggression.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: They see free markets as peaceful and blame war on the state, which Rothbard calls mass murder.

taxation-theft.rationale: Rothbard argues taxation is forcible theft because only the state raises revenue by coercion rather than gifts or sales.

harm-principle.rationale: Self-ownership grounds opposition to paternalism, though right-libertarians restrict only rights violations, which is narrower than harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are held by individuals, with strong self-ownership at the base.

conscription.rationale: Rothbard says conscription is slavery and is illegitimate.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Competition among jurisdictions and the right to secede or leave are favored, though sources do not rank them above voting.

state-as-business.rationale: Many favor privatization or competition in government services, but they would prefer to replace the state function than to run it like a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Freedom is understood as absence of coercion, and a duty to supply material means would need redistribution.

media-academia-power.rationale: The ideology does not take a position on this empirical claim about power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The doctrine is silent, and individualists reject group-based policy whichever way the empirical question goes.

organic-representation.rationale: Group representation subordinates individuals to bodies they did not choose.

total-state.rationale: The state directing all of life is the opposite of the strictly limited government that defines the view.

national-rebirth.rationale: A collectivist nationalist programme is incompatible with individual-rights doctrine.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Libertarians oppose militarism and empire and favor non-interventionism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority by oath of loyalty is arbitrary rule, not rights-based law.

bound-labor.rationale: Rothbard condemns involuntary servitude as slavery.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Right-libertarians such as Rothbard defend knowledge by reason and natural law, rejecting relativism.

universal-morality.rationale: Right-libertarianism is defended through universal natural rights knowable by reason, as in Rothbard and Nozick.

single-common-good.rationale: Libertarians reject a single collective good that overrides individual rights and the plurality of ends.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The doctrine does not address national homelands, and adherents differ.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Immigration rights are not universal in the doctrine, and a state granting special citizenship is not a rights matter.

revive-national-language.rationale: State language mandates impose costs on individuals, so they would not favor them, though not a core question.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Owners control their property, and a legally mandated vote for others overrides property rights.

school-vouchers.rationale: Friedman proposed vouchers and many accept them as a step, though Rothbard-style adherents prefer to end public funding altogether.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Right-libertarians oppose Keynesian stimulus and deficit spending.

economic-freedom.rationale: Defending capitalist economic freedom is as central as political liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: They favor impersonal rules and limited power over reliance on rulers' virtue, though not stated directly.

national-self-determination.rationale: Secession and self-government are endorsed on individual consent, though not through nation-states as such.

force-without-un.rationale: Non-interventionists reject using force abroad regardless of UN approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rationalist natural-law and Objectivist strands favor reason, but religious conservatives within the family dissent.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: They oppose welfare, but whether it should be citizen-only divides those who accept its existence.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Having rejected welfare, those who accept it as a transitional step generally prefer work conditions.

class-collaboration.rationale: Austrian economists hold that market exchange creates harmony of interests, though this is not stated in the sources opened.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Destroying property or institutions in the name of renewal is not endorsed, though ownership decides.

dominated-front.rationale: They oppose political blocs and nationalist fronts; this is inferred from general non-interventionism.

workers-nation.rationale: Organization of workers by class or nation is a collectivist frame.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Equal rights before the law do not allow law that assigns roles by sex.

ban-interest.rationale: Voluntary lending at interest is a free contract.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: State-imposed segregation restricts the contract and property rights of all.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rothbard and some strands hold that the state is a vehicle for a parasitic class, though minarchists do not.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: They oppose environmental regulation and subsidies alike, and favor production by property owners.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Free-association logic says owners decide, but they do not demand assimilation by law.

elite-replacement.rationale: The view does not hold such a conspiracy theory.

proportional-representation.rationale: The ideology is indifferent to electoral system design.

national-mission.rationale: Imposing a form of government abroad is intervention and militarism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: They stress equal legal rights and treat outcomes as results of voluntary choices.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Public choice scepticism and Rothbard's ruling-class theory lead them to distrust political elites.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: State killings and abuses are aggression, which they hold should be answerable in law.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Minarchists endorse a state limited to courts, police and military, while anarcho-capitalists want even those functions privatized.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial restrictions on marriage violate individual rights.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The rights of self-ownership are held equally by all persons.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The question is internal to Marxism and the ideology takes no position.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Property claims decide, and the label itself is not part of the doctrine.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal treatment under law fits equal rights, though they would prefer privatized personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Peaceful religious choice is not aggression.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Owners may use their property in peaceful ways, so a ban is an unjust restriction.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Public schooling is opposed in principle, and if it exists they favor religious neutrality.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The view treats state growth as the problem, not a response to external threat.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Right-libertarians treat consent as basis for legitimate authority, with anarchists saying the state fails the test.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is rejected; trade is mutually beneficial exchange.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal is aggression against persons and property.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Rothbard's axiom is that no person or group may initiate force against another's person or property.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Market competition is credited with progress, but struggle between peoples is rejected, so mixed.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Rothbard's protection of speech and assembly extends to advocacy, so parties are not outlawed.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Liberty means absence of interference; unexercised power does not take it away.

separated-powers.rationale: Limited government doctrine favors checks on state power.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined revolutionary party to rule is the opposite of the doctrine.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Institutions protect equal rights and entitlements, not priority for any class.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Privatizing public housing is welcome, though forcing a sale is not clearly aligned with property rights.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Picketing that invades property is illegitimate, but they oppose state regulation of voluntary labor action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Right-libertarians generally see institutions, such as property rights, as the main cause, though this is inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Adherents differ, with paleolibertarians saying yes and others no.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not a rights question; they would limit offices rather than choose how they are filled.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rothbard defends civil liberties without exemption for emergencies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price ceilings override voluntary exchange and cause shortages by market theory.

party-controls-media.rationale: Press freedom is among protected civil liberties.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of armed force is the opposite of limited, rights-bound government.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship rules are not a central question and adherents differ.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay levels are a minor matter, but they hold it should be left to the market, not statute.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Representatives should answer to rights and constituents, not party; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational unions concentrate coercive power and conflict with non-interventionism.

head-commands-forces.rationale: A strong executive is not favored, though minarchists differ on structure.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Internal church governance is a private matter on which the doctrine is silent.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religious rulers could punish consensual acts, which the view rejects.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Rothbard opposed state wars, but adherents differ on defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Rothbard defends speech and publishing as rights.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: They favor limits on state power, though term limits are a procedural matter.

recall-officials.rationale: Checks on officials fit limited government, but it is not central.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Right-libertarians favor non-interventionism and oppose empire.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Renting is a voluntary exchange of property.

people-in-arms.rationale: They favor private gun ownership, but the replacement of professional forces is not a settled view.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The doctrine is silent on lifestyle claims.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nation-based claims are not part of the doctrine.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold differing views.

death-penalty.rationale: Right-libertarians split between proportional retribution and distrust of state power over life.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Public school curricula are opposed in principle; this is inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: They oppose state-set curricula of any kind.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Rothbard lists pornography among consensual acts that are not crimes.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The doctrine does not decide citizenship rules.

minority-language-support.rationale: State language programmes are funded by taxation, which they oppose.

religious-exemptions.rationale: They favor minimal burdens on peaceful practice, so exemptions fit, though they would prefer to repeal the burdens for everyone.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Social pressure is non-coercive and thus not a rights issue, so no common stance.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Adherents differ on odious debt, with no clear doctrine.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The view favors free-market economics, not property transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Procedural question on which the doctrine has no view.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Economic and political freedom are held to go together.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: State aid is coerced redistribution, and charity should be voluntary.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Minarchists support defense and non-interventionists differ on nukes.

central-bank-independence.rationale: They prefer abolition, so independence is at best a lesser alternative.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is held as an absolute right, not conditional on collective good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Austrian economists called the USSR socialist, so they would reject the state-capitalist label.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Liability for proven harm replaces pre-emptive regulation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Curbing property and clergy by state action violates property and association rights.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Using force against people who leave is aggression.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Decentralization fits their view, but this is inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Reverence for a ruler contradicts equal rights and limited government.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A flat tax is preferred to progressive rates, though Rothbardians want income tax abolished.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The view requires rulers be bound by law and rights.

space-expansion.rationale: Private pursuit is allowed but a collective civilization goal is not endorsed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: No doctrine on constitutional form beyond limits.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader worship is incompatible with limited government.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are a family-law design question, and right-libertarian sources set out no common position on it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Internal to Marxism; the view is indifferent.

land-redistribution.rationale: Taking property from owners and handing it to others is theft.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claiming territory by nationality is aggression and empire.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Peaceful religious choice cannot be punished.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compelling dress is force against peaceful people.

common-currency.rationale: They favor market money and competing currencies, though a supranational state currency is not their preference.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ethnic political unions lack basis in individual rights.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Austrian methodological individualism rejects materialist historical determinism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Concentrated economic power gained peacefully is acceptable, so antitrust is state intrusion.

no-bailouts.rationale: Public funding of failing firms is redistribution and subsidy they oppose.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rights are meant to constrain majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas are state coercion and treat people as members of groups.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Free trade is central, and bloc autarky restricts it.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards in trade deals are regulation they oppose.

moral-incentives.rationale: Voluntary exchange with material incentives is the defended system.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Adherents prefer peaceful means and reject aggression, though not stated for this case.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: They oppose legal privileges but defend private inheritance, so it is not unqualified.

history-own-civilization.rationale: They oppose state-directed curricula, so this is inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Empire and rule over others is aggression.

patriotic-education.rationale: State schooling that instils loyalty is opposed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Equal rights before law rule out state racial preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: They favor market money, not a public monopoly of creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Austrian economists hold that capitalism lacks a general collapse tendency.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating influence over former colonies is empire and intervention.

delink-world-market.rationale: Free trade is defended for rich and poor countries.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Capitalist trade is not exploitation, so this Marxist thesis is rejected.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Private owners may decide whom to deal with by freedom of association and property rights, which Rothbard extends to all peaceful choices.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights as constraints on government fit, though Rothbard doubted constitutions.

elective-rulers.rationale: Consent fits election more than inheritance, though not a central point.

minority-veto.rationale: Individual consent as basis of obligation favors it, though minarchists do not accept it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Lockean tradition defends resistance to rulers who break rights.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Rights limit all lawmakers, including parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Adherents split, with Rothbard-type positions rejecting animal rights.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Use of animals as property is accepted, with humane treatment optional.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Charity is a voluntary virtue, but a duty is not enforceable.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Adherents differ between political engagement and withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The view does not hold this claim.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Rothbard's analysis holds that states rest on public acceptance cultivated by intellectuals.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Trade is positive-sum, so this dependency thesis is rejected.

native-born-offices.rationale: Equal rights before the law rule out birth restrictions.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: They oppose aid but favor foreign investment and trade.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Race- or descent-based political rank violates equal rights.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: They condemn both as extreme states, though not stated in the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Owners decide for private monuments, and the doctrine opposes public ones.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: They oppose state programmes for any group.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Equal protection against aggression applies to all.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Rights are universal, so institutions should not depend on civilization.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political army is the opposite of limited government.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages are set by exchange, and a state payment would be redistribution.

filial-duty.rationale: A private moral matter on which the doctrine is silent.

office-by-exam.rationale: How civil-service posts are filled is a procedural matter the rights-and-property doctrine does not settle.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Property owners may sell to anyone.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Marriage as contract may be ended by the parties.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatizing state pension systems is a standard policy, though many want abolition rather than mandated accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Property by homesteading and transfer is permanent, not by use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Legislative control of spending is a procedural detail; the doctrine cares more about how much the state may take than who approves it.

single-official-language.rationale: State enforcement of language restricts peaceful choices.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Owners may sell to anyone, though some restrictionists differ.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Discrimination is a matter of intent and rights, not outcomes.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Intervention against an ally is aggression.

corporate-influence.rationale: They object to special privileges obtained through the state, though they blame the state.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Restricting voluntary funding and speech is state interference.

residents-only-property.rationale: Owners may sell to anyone and local limits violate property rights.

job-guarantee.rationale: State jobs for all means taxation and planning.

democratic-peace.rationale: Factual claim, though they oppose war to spread democracy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rothbard treats the state as an agency of coercion that lacks special authority.

non-intervention.rationale: Libertarians support a foreign policy of non-interventionism.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is a private matter.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The view does not hold conspiracy claims about groups.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: State benefits for marriage are redistribution, and marriage is a contract.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Limiting state secrecy fits limited government, though inferred.

local-production.rationale: Free trade and the division of labor are defended.

informal-organisation.rationale: Organization form is a strategy matter.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tribute systems are imperial and coercive.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Decentralization and limited taxation make this likely.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The view rejects common ownership of production, though it defends personal property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Rothbardians oppose communism strongly, but by persuasion and not by war.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: They oppose a publicly funded system as such.

religion-illusion.rationale: Objectivists say yes, but others disagree.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Capitalism is defended as productive and beneficial.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: They hold that capitalism and equal rights are enough.

socialized-care.rationale: Public services require tax and compulsion.

purge-loanwords.rationale: State language rules restrict peaceful speech.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Voluntary communes are permitted but not prescribed as the form of society.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-directed settlement violates property and freedom of movement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Capitalism is defended as the sound basis.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Ownership comes from homesteading and transfer, not historical or religious ties.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Right-libertarianism does not hold such denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Consensual acts with no victim are not crimes for Rothbard.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Speech and religion are protected from punishment.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious doctrine on which the view takes no position.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Armed removal on religious grounds is aggression.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Majority-style direct decisions in workplaces violate property rights.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Adherents split between private freedom and rejecting state categories.

assisted-dying.rationale: Self-ownership grounds control over one's own body and life.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The view sits on the right of economic issues, though some libertarians see themselves as neither.

alienated-labor.rationale: Wage labor is a voluntary exchange.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Rights are held to be natural and reasoned, not divinely delegated, though some strands are religious.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents differ over rules in state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: They favor freedom of contract, though not on this question specifically.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Minarchists keep defense while anarcho-capitalists privatize it.

rich-first.rationale: They accept unequal outcomes from non-coercive exchange.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Non-interventionism favors staying out of blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Not endorsed, but not a rights question.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Credit on market terms is the defended system.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: They oppose international lenders but favor austerity.

property-franchise.rationale: Equal rights are favored, though some think voting should be limited.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Eco-feminist framing is not part of the doctrine.

reification.rationale: Market exchange is not alienating on their view.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Property rights apply and speech freedom is not defined by ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law is a defining liberal principle of Hayek and the tradition.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency of state action fits limited government.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotts are legitimate speech but promoting bigotry is not endorsed.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Selected groups deciding for others has no basis in rights.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Concentrated economic power is acceptable if arising by non-coercive means.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Equal treatment, though adherents are divided on armed forces.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: State promotion of belief is opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists would privatize them, and minarchists keep them.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Redistribution is held counter-productive and private charity is the alternative, as with Nozick.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: They do not give public policy goals priority.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marriage terms are a private contract between spouses, so the doctrine takes no stance on how authority is divided.

abolish-ip.rationale: Rothbard opposed patents while others defend IP.

uniformed-youth.rationale: State drilling of youth is conscription-like.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Adherents split between non-interventionist wariness of weapons and minarchist support for defense, with no settled doctrine.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Rothbard bans initiation of force, so defense is legitimate.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: A nationalist claim not in the doctrine.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: This is a question of social theory outside the rights-and-property doctrine, which has no standard position.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: This is an internal debate in feminist theory that right-libertarian sources do not address.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: They oppose state cults of nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Politics is about rights, not spiritual struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The doctrine concerns individual rights, not the role of a national homeland for a diaspora, so there is no common view.

culture-before-state.rationale: Right-libertarians do not rank cultural renewal against state-building, as they seek less state, not a nation-building order.

god-not-male.rationale: How God is described is a theological question the political doctrine does not address.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Judging religious texts by a feminist test is a matter for religions, not a question the doctrine addresses.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Property and trade are open to all.

independent-unions.rationale: Voluntary unions free of the state fit.

second-chamber.rationale: A second chamber adds a check on lawmaking, which suits limited-government thinking, though constitutional design is not central.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Governance by assembly does not protect individual rights.

family-wage.rationale: Wages are set by market exchange.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Tax funding is opposed, though private research is welcome.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Privacy against state monitoring follows from rights.

online-anonymity.rationale: Privacy against state follows from rights.

person-over-state.rationale: Rights act as side constraints that persons may not be used as means.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Whether humans have a spiritual nature is outside the doctrine, and adherents range from religious to atheist.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: They favor decentralization, so revocable power is disfavored.

dense-cities.rationale: Which settlement pattern is better for the environment is an empirical question the doctrine leaves to markets and property owners.

racial-pride.rationale: Personal views not a doctrine point.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Nation-definition is not a rights question.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The doctrine has no claim that foreign powers plot to partition countries, and its non-interventionism does not imply it.

pollution-taxes.rationale: They prefer liability to taxes, though Chicago economists accept them.

future-generations.rationale: Obligations to hand on the Earth undamaged are not framed in rights terms; adherents rely on property liability and differ on the wider duty.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Open treaties fit the distrust of unaccountable state power, though the doctrine is not specific about diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Free movement of capital follows from property rights.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Gun rights and private defense are defended.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Conscription is slavery and wars are condemned.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Individual contract is the default and compulsory bargaining is opposed.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Top-ups are redistribution, though some accept Friedman-style supplements.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Anarchists agree but minarchists do not.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Voluntary communities of many kinds fit a rights-based framework.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Market valuation is accepted but views differ.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Natural rights are tied to human nature.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Religious pluralism claims are outside the political doctrine, and adherents hold many different views.

farm-price-support.rationale: Subsidy and price supports are opposed.

ban-fgm.rationale: It is aggression against a person.

one-language-many-names.rationale: What a language should be called is a linguistic and cultural question with no libertarian doctrine behind it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Property-rights liability for harm replaces agency regulation.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Official status for any hereditary body is not favored.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Punishment should be proportionate to the crime.

voter-id.rationale: Voting procedures are not a core matter; some adherents favor integrity measures and others distrust adding state requirements.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Equal treatment of religious interpretations fits the view that the state should not privilege any belief.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Adherents differ on whether a democracy defined by elections alone is worth the name when majorities can override rights.

premarital-sex.rationale: Consensual acts are not state matters.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Cutting communications restricts speech and association of peaceful people, which Rothbard treats as protected liberties.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Friedman proposed it, though Rothbardians reject it.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal rights before the law cover equal voting and office-holding, though some adherents doubt voting itself matters much.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The doctrine does not hold this claim, and libertarians treat religious observance as a private choice unless force is used.

race-social-construct.rationale: This is a scientific and social-theory claim on which the rights-based doctrine takes no position.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Original acquisition by claiming and working unowned resources is a central principle of the view.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Adherents split between holding leaders accountable for aggression and distrusting supranational courts as new state powers.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Doctrines about scripture are private beliefs on which the political doctrine is silent.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Border questions depend on consent and property claims in the doctrine, which gives no general rule on colonial boundaries.

simple-living.rationale: Living simply is a voluntary lifestyle choice that the rights-based doctrine neither promotes nor forbids.

close-ties-china.rationale: Trade with all, but no policy.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Wikipedia states that right-libertarians reject the left-libertarian claim that natural resources belong to everyone and hold they can be appropriated with little or no payment.

self-ownership.rationale: The SEP describes very strong self-ownership rights as the foundation of right-libertarianism.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Taxation is theft, so less is better.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: They prefer cuts, but targeting is a lesser evil.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The view opposes state favors, and concentrated power is fine only when non-coercive.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Politics based on religion violates neutrality.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Combining technology with tradition is a cultural choice, and adherents differ between modernist and paleolibertarian outlooks.

national-resource-control.rationale: Private owners hold resources, not national or foreign states.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The SEP states that right-libertarian distributive justice is historical, so redistribution is justified only to correct wrongful takings.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Taxation is held to be coercion, and Rothbard calls it theft, so a new tax on financial trades is rejected in principle.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Most right-libertarians hold that other causes such as policy and culture now matter more, but adherents are split, so this is inferred from their general scepticism of structural claims.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Natural-rights libertarianism holds that rights precede and limit legislation, so rights-violating rules lack authority; inferred, since strands differ.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Libertarians welcome automation produced by markets but reject society deciding to automate as policy or redistributing its gains; inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Right-libertarians favour non-interventionism and competition among jurisdictions, but the question of organising world power is not a core issue and adherents are split.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The labour theory conflicts with the subjective-value, market-price view of the Austrian and Chicago wings, and with justifying unequal rewards by voluntary exchange.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Right-libertarians are individualist and distrust collective national loyalties and state-driven worker politics; inferred, adherents split.

material-over-identity.rationale: Right-libertarians reject a left-wing programme either way; they would put individual rights ahead of both workers' interests and identity politics. Inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Right-libertarians hold that state direction and one-party rule violate property and non-aggression, whatever role markets play.

missingStatements.text: Whether a distribution of wealth is just depends on how it came about, not on how equal it is.
missingStatements.rationale: The SEP states that right-libertarian distributive justice is historical, so redistribution is justified only to correct wrongful takings.

notes: Anarcho-capitalists and minarchists split on state-related statements (state-harmful, police, courts, armed forces); mainstream answers sit between them.
